https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: 1:28 Iran retaliates after US missile strike reportedly hits wedding - video US-Israel war on Iran Iran accuses US of ‘war crime’ after missile blast kills four people at wedding Blast also injures 68 guests at the wedding in southern Iran, prompting fears of escalation in hostilities Middle East crisis live – latest updates William Christou in Beirut Wed 2 Sep 2026 11.19 EDT First published on Wed 2 Sep 2026 07.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Iran has accused the US of a war crime after a missile blast killed at least four people and injured 68 who were attending a wedding at a private home in a coastal city of southern Iran, as the fresh exchange of strikes prompted fears of a wider renewal of hostilities. Iranian media said that the wedding ceremony was being held in a home in the city of Kuhestak, Hormozgan province, late on Tuesday when a US missile struck, with shrapnel and debris from the strike killing and injuring people. Among the dead was a four-year-old child, Amir-Ali Karimi, and a 16-year-old, Mohammad Mollahi. “It’s a terrible thing. I’m extremely worried and upset about what happened – really upset,” Ali Mollahi, the father of the bride, told Mehr News . View image in fullscreen Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson called the US attack on Kuhestak a ‘war crime’. Photograph: Masoud Mohamadi/Tasnim News/AFP/Getty Images A video of the aftermath shows colourful wedding streamers and decorations strewn across the ground, and shoes abandoned in the rush to escape the attack. “You wicked people have attacked people’s homes and turned their wedding ceremony into a funeral,” said a man filming the aftermath of the strike, shared by Fars news agency. The deputy of the provincial government, Ahmad Nafisi, said first responders had headed immediately to the scene and transferred the wounded to the hospitals. Iran’s foreign ministry spokesperson called the US attack a “war crime” and said Iran “will respond to these savage crimes with firmness”. The chief Iranian negotiator, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, said the attack had killed families with children, and called the US the “great Satan”. “If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan and kills like Satan, it’s Satan. Shields a junior Satan that does the same? It’s THE Great Satan,” Ghalibaf said in a post on X. View image in fullscreen Footage of the aftermath of the strike shows a caved-in roof, blown-out windows and ground riddled with debris. Photograph: Iranian Red Crescent/AFP/Getty Images The US attacks followed strikes on Sunday, ending a month-long uneasy truce between the US and Iran, and appeared to signal a resumption of another cycle of escalation. US Central Command (Centcom) said the overnight strikes focused on Iranian military targets, including air defence sites, radars and maritime assets. Iran responded by launching drones and missiles on US bases across the Middle East, including in Bahrain, Kuwait and the UAE. Iran’s military spokesperson, Lt Col Ebrahim Zolfaghari, vowed “heavier, broader, and more crushing and devestating” retaliation. Videos of the aftermath of the strike show a caved-in roof, blown-out windows and ground riddled with debris, as well as walls pockmarked with what appeared to be holes from shrapnel. Footage from a nearby hospital showed women in wedding attire watching as injured children were being treated . “When we arrived there, an explosion occurred. It was very intense. Bricks, stones and cement hit me in the face and head, and many others were injured,” a child who was injured at the wedding told the state-affiliated Fars news agency. View image in fullscreen The strike on Kuhestak appeared to signal another cycle of escalation in the US-Iran conflict. Photograph: Masoud Mohamadi/Tasnim News/AFP/Getty Images A woman with her hands decorated in henna for the nuptials posted a video on Instagram after the attack, saying “my hands and feet are still shaking”. A spokesperson for Centcom, Tim Hawkins, said the US was aware of reports of civilian casualties, but the “US military never targets civilians, unlike the [Iranian Revolutionary Guards Corps]”. ‘Her head was broken’: parents at Iranian school bombed by US describe their worst day Read more In February, a strike on an elementary school killed at least 156 people, including more than 120 schoolchildren. Independent investigations concluded that the US likely carried out the strike with the assistance of AI, though the US government said the incident remained under investigation. Pictures of shrapnel collected at the site of Tuesday’s attack were published on Iranian state media, and appeared to show the internal components of US munitions . Trevor Ball, an independent weapons analyst, identified some of the remnants as belonging to the Standoff Land Attack Missile-Expanded Response (Slam-Er) missile, which is made by the US weapons company Boeing. The Slam-Er is a 1,500-pound, GPS-guided missile touted by Boeing to be “extremely accurate” . It was unclear if the home where the wedding was being held was struck directly, or if a missile hit close to the home and debris from the strike hit the home and its occupants. CCTV footage captured at least six strikes in the area within a minute. A separate strike appeared to hit a communications tower about 150 metres away from the home. Authorities said that several “telecommunications and internet towers and sites were also seriously damaged in the latest strikes”. View image in fullscreen A separate strike on Kuhestak hit a communications tower about 150 metres from the home where the wedding was being held. Photograph: Masoud Mohammadi/AP The US has been targeting communications and radar infrastructure along Iran’s coast to try to stop its blockade on the strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint which prior to the US-Iran war was a transit point for at least 20% of the world’s oil supply. Iran has virtually closed the strait since the start of the Iran war, frustrating the US president, Donald Trump, who is facing a midterm election with expensive gas prices and knock-on inflation across the board. In recent weeks, the US has focused on trying to degrade Iran’s capacity to strike ships transiting the strait to reopen the waterway for traffic. http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/05/us-pe.text: US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to visit Kyiv and Moscow this weekend, armed with a "proposal to end the war," US President Donald Trump has announced, in the latest push to break a diplomatic deadlock over the war in Ukraine."I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They've done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we'll do it," Trump told reporters on Friday.The pair are expected in Moscow on Saturday before heading to Kyiv on Sunday, in what will be their first visits to the Ukrainian capital since Trump returned to the White house in January last year.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the planned visit to Ukraine in a post on X."We need to look for real options for how to move this war toward an end," Zelenskyy wrote. "We will see what proposals Steve and Jared bring and what they are told in Moscow in response".He added that Ukrainian forces would ensure the "normal functioning of Russian airspace" to ensure the envoys could make the trip to Moscow safely.Zelenskyy had warned airlines and insurers on Tuesday that Russian airspace would "effectively be closing" due to the scale of Ukrainian drone operations making flying unsafe.But the Ukrainian leader said Ukraine would hold off on strikes while Witkoff and Kushner made the trip, while calling on Moscow to do the same."We are looking out for them, not for Russia. There will be no air strikes from our side, and Russia must do the same, ensuring there are no air strikes from its side for the time needed to hold these talks and handle the logistical matters related to this American visit," he wrote on social media.Russian strikes kill four overnightThe announcement came as Russian strikes on the city of Kamianske in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region killed four overnight, per local authorities.Oleksandr Hanzha, the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Oblast Military Administration, said five people were also injured in the strikes, which hit an industrial facility.On Friday, Zelenskyy announced that a Russian drone had also hit the headquarters of Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) in central Kyiv, adding that it had been "aimed directly" at the head of the agency's office.In response to the attack, he said he had ordered the SBU to carry out an "appropriate, tangible response and, where possible, one that mirrors this strike."

https://www.politico.eu/article/russia-v.text: BRUSSELS — Top European officials are increasingly alarmed that Russia could stage drone or missile attacks against NATO countries as Moscow steps up its hybrid campaign across the continent. Germany is preparing hospitals for a possible conflict , Lithuania has updated evacuation plans and NATO troops are exercising in the Baltic region, while Belarusian forces have staged large maneuvers near Lithuania. On Thursday, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned Moscow could send drones or missiles into the territory of NATO countries supporting Ukraine in “the next few months.” Advertisement Advertisement The warnings underscore a growing sense of anxiety in Europe amid fast-proliferating incidents of airspace violations and sabotage attempts in recent months. NATO allies have repeatedly said they see the attacks as pressure from the Kremlin to reduce their support for Ukraine but have muted their response over fears of escalation. French President Emmanuel Macron summoned party leaders and 2027 presidential candidates for an emergency meeting on Friday to talk about Ukraine, Iran and the growing energy crisis. He called Tusk’s warnings “sound and well-documented” as he announced a new critical infrastructure protection plan, adding: “In recent weeks … the Russian hybrid threat against Europeans and France has intensified.” Guillaume Lacroix, leader of the Radical Party of the Left, left the meeting saying : “At the age of 50, I have rarely felt such vertigo.” “It is no coincidence that the Polish prime minister is speaking out so strongly,” Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said Friday. “We need to take that warning very seriously … we must consistently demonstrate that we do not accept this and that we will take action if necessary.” On Thursday, Finnish President Alexander Stubb told his country it was “worth mentally preparing for something to happen” including sabotage and Russian drones. Advertisement Advertisement Moscow is also ramping up its bellicose rhetoric ahead of Russia's legislative election this weekend that is widely expected to keep President Vladimir Putin's United Russia party in power. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov this week warned Europe it would face a “very short” war if NATO allies attempted to attack the country. “Russia has stepped up the pace of its activities — we need to remain vigilant,” said one senior European defense official, who was granted anonymity to speak freely. “This may be seen as a manifestation of a broader trend ... we have seen similar warnings before, and there may well be more to come.” So far, the latest incidents haven't prompted any additional multilateral responses, a second senior European defense official said. But “we are monitoring closely,” they added. Staying the course On Friday, German and Swedish forces carried out joint exercises near the strategic Swedish island of Gotland , just weeks after NATO allies carried out unannounced exercises near the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. In recent weeks, NATO jets shot down a Russian drone over Lithuania, a Russian ship fired flares at a Danish military helicopter and Germany blamed an attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport on a suspected Russian spy . Advertisement Advertisement U.S. intelligence reports in August warned that Moscow was planning a limited assault on a NATO country in the coming years. CIA Director John Ratcliffe warned Russian officials in Moscow late last month not to escalate conflict with NATO allies, in particular Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, in response to Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Yet it remains unclear whether the latest warnings are based on fresh intelligence. On Friday, Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys said Vilnius had “the same intelligence” as Tusk “about a possible foreign-flag operation” but suggested that dated back to July. “I see the public statements of politicians about this as part of a coordinated campaign to warn Russia not to make stupid decisions and not to try to do something thinking that it will not reach [NATO’s mutual defense clause] Article 5 and will not be washed away,” he said. Allies have not formally been briefed on any new intelligence inside NATO, according to two alliance diplomats, and NATO has so far not changed its threat assessment. “At this time, we see no imminent threat of attack,” said a NATO official speaking on behalf of the organization, adding: “But we cannot not be naive or complacent, and we must make sure NATO remains strong in the years ahead.” Advertisement Advertisement Ed Arnold, a former NATO official and adviser at the D Group consultancy, said the warnings could also be designed to raise public awareness of threats and to “pre-bunk” false flag attacks before they take place. A senior NATO military official said that Russia may be lashing out because of its difficulties in defeating Ukraine. “It therefore may incorrectly perceive the only way out is through increasing its hybrid campaign — that’s a losing proposition, because we are ready to respond.” Between January and August, there were 100 officially attributed hybrid incidents across Europe compared to 60 during the same period last year, according to the Ukraine-based Sahaidachnyi Security Center think tank — with a particularly sharp rise in airspace violations. A senior NATO official said the real number was “easily 200 plus” not counting cyberattacks — of which there are “thousands” each month against the military alliance’s Brussels headquarters alone. “Numbers are up, severity is up, [Russia’s] risk appetite is up,” they said.
